text: Given Autotask answers GET /Tickets/{t}/Attachments/{a} with {"items":[record]}, when autotask_get_ticket_attachment is called without includeData, then the metadata is returned and there is no error.
Given the parent-scoped GET answers 404 and GET /TicketAttachments/{a} answers {"items":[record]}, when called with includeData false, then the metadata is returned.
Given GET /TicketAttachments/{a} answers {"items":[record with data]}, when called with includeData=true, then the result contains data.
Given the same items-shaped answer and maxInlineBase64Bytes smaller than the content, when called with includeData=true, then data is absent and dataOmittedReason and dataLength are present.
Given an items-shaped record whose parentID is another ticket, when called with this ticket id, then the result is a not_found error.
Given Autotask answers {"items":[]}, when called, then the result is a not_found error.
Given Autotask answers {"item":{record}}, when called with includeData false and true, then both succeed as before.
Given an items-shaped answer for a ticket note attachment, when autotask_get_ticket_note_attachment is called, then metadata and data are returned.
Given items holds two records, when called with the id of the second, then that record is returned.
On a real Autotask zone, read a PDF attachment listed by autotask_search_ticket_attachments with includeData false and then true; both return the record and the second returns the file content.
precond: Real Autotask zone credentials and a ticket with a PDF attachment
steps: Call autotask_get_ticket_attachment for a listed attachment with includeData false
expect: Both calls return the attachment record without error; the second also returns the file content (base64 data)
